free_tier.stated: Free plan, USD 0 a month: 1,000 requests a month at 1 request a second, no credit card; the response is the full one, including the security and company fields that paid plans gate.
free_tier.notes: Each IP in a request counts as one credit, and credits are counted per request, not per successful response. Past the monthly credits the API answers HTTP 422, and past 1 request a second HTTP 429. Starter is USD 17 a month billed annually (USD 19 paid monthly).

per_object_cap.stated: one IP address per request; the product page says no separate batch endpoint is needed

interface_detail: GET https://ipgeolocation.abstractapi.com/v1/ with api_key, an optional ip_address (IPv4 or IPv6; the caller's address when omitted) and an optional fields list; JSON over HTTPS, TLS 1.2 or greater
tooling: any HTTP client; vendor libraries for Python, PHP and Node.js
chaining: 1,000 keyed lookups a month, each returning location, time zone, flag, currency, ASN, company and security fields, at 1 request a second. Bulk path: none; the single-IP call is looped at the plan's rate limit, and a browser bulk tool takes a pasted list with no key

limits.value: 1,000 requests a month on the Free plan
1 request a second on the Free plan; HTTP 429 above it

binding_note: 1,000 requests a month is used up long before 1 request a second can matter.

identity_cost.detail: an email address and password with a verification link, or Google sign-in; no credit card on the free plan

reliability_note: Past the free monthly credits the API answers HTTP 422, and past 1 request a second HTTP 429; a request for an invalid IP still uses one credit.
confidence_note: The pricing, product, documentation and sign-up pages were read on 2026-11-02, and a keyless call to the API answered HTTP 400 naming api_key as required; no keyed lookup was made, so the quota and the rate limit are as published.

evidence.proved: a free plan that has used its credits is answered HTTP 422
evidence.quote: | 422 | Quota reached | The request was aborted due to insufficient API credits. (Free plans) |

evidence.proved: above 1 request a second a free plan is answered HTTP 429
evidence.quote: | 429 | Too many requests | The request was aborted due to the number of allowed requests per second being reached. This happens on free plans as requests are limited to 1 per second. |

evidence.proved: every submitted IP uses one credit, and a failed request still uses it
evidence.quote: A note on metered billing: Each individual IP you submit counts as a credit used. Credits are also counted per request, not per successful response.
